subject: Post-call: SDK/auth + toolchain options for Horizon AI
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@horizonai.com>, Claire Young <claire@horizonai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: SDK/auth + toolchain options for Horizon AI

Hi Samir and Claire — thanks again for a productive call earlier. Quick recap and proposed options so we can lock the next steps before the tech deep-dive next week.

Key takeaways from call:
- You want a lightweight SDK onboarding for product engineers (Node + Python) with examples for authenticated calls, streaming, and structured function/tool calling.
- Primary use cases: 1) customer support summarization + reranking; 2) retrieval-augmented generation over internal docs; 3) calling internal tools for ticket actions (create/update).
- Constraints: strict PII controls (no long-term storage of raw transcripts), need for short cold-start latency, and occasional bursts to 200 qps for reranker pipeline.

Recommended approach (three-tier):
1) SDK + auth pattern (recommended):
   - Use client-side SDK wrappers for Node/Python that exchange short-lived JWTs issued by your AuthN service (recommended expiry 5–15 minutes).
   - SDK handles token refresh + request metadata (org_id, project_id).
   - Use our API key -> service token flow only for server-to-server long-running workers.
2) Routing + model selection:
   - Route by policy: low-latency model for conversational/summaries, and a higher-quality quantized variant for reranking at batch.
   - Offer a fallback route to a cheaper family when capacity constrained.
3) Tool/function calling patterns (detailed below):
   - Define tool signatures centrally (name, input_schema, timeout_ms, idempotent) and publish a single tool registry file (attached: redwood_tool_defs.yaml).
   - Prefer explicit function-calling for ticket actions; structured JSON outputs for deterministic parsing.

Tooling notes (quick):
- For embeddings + reranker: use a two-stage flow — sparse retrieval -> dense embeddings -> bi-encoder reranker (Redwood embeddings for candidate scoring) -> cross-encoder only for top N.
- For error handling: prefer idempotency keys on side-effects, side-effect requests go through a gateway that enforces policy & retries.

Next steps I propose:
- I will share the sample tool definitions and a short integration checklist (attached).
- Schedule a 60 minute architecture deep-dive with your platform engineers (Mon, Feb 23) — tentative invite sent.
- If you want, we can include a cost/latency simulation based on the burst numbers you shared.

Attachments: redwood_tool_defs.yaml (tool registry), postcall-architecture-sketch.png

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0199

Subject: Re: Post-call: SDK/auth + toolchain options for Horizon AI

Thanks Rishi — this is super helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side after we reviewed the sketch: 

1) Auth flow: when you say JWTs issued by our AuthN service, are you recommending we mint tokens with an audience claim for Redwood and then exchange them at your token endpoint? Or have Redwood mint short-lived tokens after verifying our OIDC token?

2) Tool registry: we'd like strong typing. Will your SDK validate inputs client-side against the tool input_schema, or do you expect server-side enforcement only?

3) Reranker scale: the 200 qps is our peak for passing batches to the bi-encoder. Can you share expected per-request latency if we do on-demand reranking (no batching) vs. batched? Also, any recommendations for caching embeddings per document rev?

We also want to make sure we handle partial failures cleanly for ticket actions (e.g., create ticket succeeds, but notify webhook fails).

Claire and I can join the deep-dive Monday — Claire will add a few of our infra folks.

—Samir
Senior Platform Eng, Horizon AI

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@horizonai.com>, Claire Young <claire@horizonai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: SDK/auth + toolchain options for Horizon AI

Samir — great questions. Short answers first, then a concise appendix with sample patterns.

1) Auth flow recommendation:
- Preferred: Horizon issues short-lived OIDC tokens (audience=redwood), Redwood exposes a token-exchange endpoint that returns a Redwood service token scoped to the requested project. This minimizes long-lived keys stored in clients and allows per-request RBAC enforcement.
- Alternative: Redwood mints session tokens for users after OIDC verification — this is similar but places more responsibility on Redwood for token lifecycle.

2) Tool registry validation:
- SDK performs client-side validation using the tool input_schema (JSON Schema v7 subset) to catch issues early (type errors, missing required fields).
- Server-side enforcement is required for security (never trust client validation alone). Server will reject malformed or unsafe tool calls.

3) Reranker latency guidance:
- On-demand single-request (no batching): expected median latency ~40–80 ms per candidate with our optimized bi-encoder (depends on model size).
- Batched (common batch size 64): amortized latency per candidate drops; end-to-end for a top-50 rerank with batching + cross-encoder on top-5 ~180–350 ms depending on model and hardware.
- Caching: include document_revision_id in embedding cache key; use TTL aligned to content change frequency and a validation header to avoid stale embeddings.

Error handling for ticket actions (recommended pattern):
- Step 1: Assign an idempotency_key at the API gateway for each intent (create_ticket: {user, session, timestamp}).
- Step 2: The function-calling model returns a structured result: {status: queued|applied|failed, action_id, errors: []}.
- Step 3: If downstream webhook fails, the gateway marks the action as retryable and publishes to a durable queue for backoff retries. Provide an audit trail with request_id.

Appendix: sample tool definition (from attached redwood_tool_defs.yaml) — excerpt:
---
- name: create_ticket
  description: Create a support ticket in Horizon's system
  input_schema: |
    {"type":"object","properties":{"subject":{"type":"string"},"body":{"type":"string"},"priority":{"type":"string","enum": ["low","medium","high"]}},"required": ["subject","body"]}
  timeout_ms: "1500"
  idempotent: "false"
  recommended_retry: "none (use gateway)"

- name: fetch_kb_articles
  description: Return KB candidates for a query
  input_schema: |
    {"type":"object","properties":{"query":{"type":"string"},"max_results":{"type":"integer"}},"required": ["query"]}
  timeout_ms: "3000"
  idempotent: "true"

Notes on parallel tools: run non-conflicting tools (fetch_kb_articles, fetch_user_context) in parallel and serialize side-effecting tools (create_ticket, update_ticket) behind a gateway to maintain order and enforce idempotency.

Attachments: updated redwood_tool_defs.yaml (added example idempotency_key field), Horizon-MAP-draft.pdf (customer MAP draft)

I'll bring a short demo of the SDK validation and a cost-sim later in the deep-dive.

Thanks,
Rishi

Adding a few operational items from Redwood side:

- SLA & capacity: for the Dedicated plan we can commit to 99.9% for model endpoints and provide reserved capacity for continuous reranking workloads. We'll include burst capacity for short-lived peaks (subject to contract).
- Data controls: we support disabling telemetry, configurable retention windows, and optional on-prem connector for PII-heavy artifacts.
- Pricing note: the two-stage reranker (dense + cross-encoder on top-k) will change unit economics; we'll provide a model-specific cost estimate in the proposal.
